title: Persistent Fermi Pockets and Robust Electron Pairing in Lightly Doped CuO2 Planes of Cuprate Superconductors
claims: Spatially resolved laser ARPES finds Fermi pockets centred at (π/2, π/2) from the inner CuO2 planes of n = 5–8 Bi-based multilayer intergrowths, with hole dopings from 0.007 to 0.088.
The lightly doped CuO2 plane is intrinsically metallic, with an abrupt transition from the Mott insulator upon an infinitesimal amount of doping.

The innermost-plane (IP0) pockets are gapless while the second-innermost-plane (IP1) pockets show an anisotropic, d-wave-like gap of up to about 33 meV, indicating robust electron pairing down to p = 0.02.
This electron pairing coexists with, and may be facilitated by, strong antiferromagnetic order.
The inner planes are shielded from disorder, so insulating behaviour reported in single- and bilayer cuprates should be re-evaluated as a disorder effect.
A mean-field t–U model with one parameter set, varying only the chemical potential, describes all observed IP0 and IP1 pockets.
summary: Using spatially resolved laser ARPES on Bi2223 crystals, the authors locate n = 5–8 intergrowth regions and report hole pockets in the inner CuO2 planes with dopings 0.007–0.088, gapless on the innermost plane and with an anisotropic gap of up to ~33 meV on the second-innermost plane. They interpret this as an intrinsic metallic state at vanishing doping and as electron pairing coexisting with strong antiferromagnetic order, and describe the pockets with a mean-field t–U model in which only the chemical potential varies.
strengths: Spatially resolved ARPES with two-dimensional momentum acquisition gives phase-selective access to n = 5–8 Bi-based intergrowths that are not available as single crystals.
The data quality is high, with clearly resolved concentric pockets (Fig. 1b–g) and well-defined quasiparticle peaks along the entire IP0 pocket (Fig. 2f).

Pocket geometry, angular spectral-weight distribution and the right/left weight ratio are treated systematically across layer number, host doping and planes (Figs. 1h–j, 2g, 2h), extending the doping range well beyond earlier reports.
A single mean-field t–U parameter set with only the chemical potential varied reproduces all pocket shapes, an economical description (Fig. 4a–f).

issues.claim: IP1 gap indicates robust electron pairing
issues.headline: Nothing shows the IP1 gap is a superconducting pairing gap
issues.issue: All gap data are taken at 15 K only and extracted from symmetrized EDCs, which assume particle–hole symmetry and produce an apparent gap whenever the band does not reach EF (pseudogap, AFM or hybridization gap, band top just below EF). This removes the information needed to distinguish a pairing gap, so 'robust electron pairing' and the AFM+SC region of Fig. 4h are not established; the Tc applicable to each intergrowth region is also unclear.

evidence.quote: These observations suggest that electron pairing can occur at very low doping levels in the presence of strong antiferromagnetic order.

issues.fix: Measure the IP1 gap versus temperature in at least one region through the relevant Tc, show particle–hole symmetric Bogoliubov behaviour (back-bending at kF or thermally populated states above EF in unsymmetrized, Fermi–Dirac-divided EDCs), and show the IP1 dispersion along θ = 90° to demonstrate kF is crossed and the gap minimum sits at the crossing. Otherwise replace 'pairing' with 'energy gap'.
issues.fix_scoped: These observations show that an anisotropic energy gap, whose origin remains to be established, opens on the IP1 pockets at doping levels as low as 0.02 in the presence of strong antiferromagnetic order.

edit_scoped.before: These observations suggest that electron pairing can occur at very low doping levels in the presence of strong antiferromagnetic order.
edit_scoped.after: These observations show that an anisotropic energy gap, whose origin remains to be established, opens on the IP1 pockets at doping levels as low as 0.02 in the presence of strong antiferromagnetic order.

issues.claim: IP1 pairing at p = 0.02 facilitated by AF order
issues.headline: Interlayer proximity or hybridization could produce the IP1 gap
issues.issue: IP1 sits next to the more heavily doped, superconducting outer plane while IP0 is further away, so a gap induced by interlayer coupling would explain the IP0-gapless/IP1-gapped contrast and the non-monotonic gap versus doping without intrinsic pairing at p = 0.02. Weak interlayer hopping is cited rather than measured, the Fig. 4 model treats each layer independently, and the gap is largest near the major-axis vertices where the IP1 pocket approaches the IP0 and outer-plane sheets, as a hybridization gap would be.

evidence.quote: Since the inner layers in our multilayer cuprates are underdoped or heavily underdoped, the interlayer hopping between the inner layers is rather weak.

issues.fix: Compare IP1 gaps in 7/8-layer regions (IP1 next to IP2) with 5/6-layer regions at similar doping, correlate the IP1 gap with the OP gap in the same region, show the gap versus momentum distance from IP0 and OP sheets, and compute a multilayer tight-binding model with interlayer hopping constrained by measured band separations and pairing only on OP.
issues.fix_scoped: Whether the IP1 gap is intrinsic or induced by coupling to the adjacent superconducting planes remains to be determined; if intrinsic, these results would indicate that electron pairing can coexist with strong antiferromagnetic correlations.

edit_scoped.before: These results indicate that electron pairing can coexist with, or even be facilitated by, strong antiferromagnetic correlations.
edit_scoped.after: Whether the IP1 gap is intrinsic or induced by coupling to the adjacent superconducting planes remains to be determined; if intrinsic, these results would indicate that electron pairing can coexist with strong antiferromagnetic correlations.

issues.claim: Pockets assigned to n = 5–8 and to IP0/IP1/IP2
issues.headline: Layer-number and plane assignment rests only on sheet counting and pocket sizes
issues.issue: The assignment of regions to n = 5, 6, 7 or 8 and of sheets to IP0, IP1 or IP2 relies on Fermi-surface counting and pocket-size ratios, with no structural identification or phase-purity check; since per-layer doping is what is measured, the argument is partly circular. A ~10 µm spot on ~50 µm regions in crystals with n = 1–9 intergrowths varying on finer scales may average several phases, so superposed sheets could be mistaken for one phase or a pocket misassigned, which would undermine the IP0/IP1 contrast.

evidence.quote: The assignment of each Fermi surface pattern to a specific intergrowth phase was made by analyzing the number of Fermi surface sheets, their momentum-space distribution, and corresponding doping levels, as detailed in the main text.

issues.fix: Show the evidence for every region (Table S1) with IP0/IP1 area ratios and uncertainties, real-space maps with spot footprint and sheet-area variation and spectra near boundaries, explain how n = 5 is excluded from n = 6 with a missing sheet, apply a doping sum rule, and where possible cross-check with micro-XRD, post-ARPES STEM/TEM or kz dependence.
issues.fix_scoped: Based on the number of Fermi surface sheets and the relative IP0 pocket sizes, we tentatively attribute the results in Fig. 1b-d to the five-layer cuprates Bi2245 and the result in Fig. 1e to the six-layer cuprate Bi2256, since the IP0 Fermi pocket in Fig. 1e is nearly half the size of that in Fig. 1c; an independent structural identification of these regions is not available.

edit_scoped.before: Based on these observations, we can attribute the results in Fig. 1b-d to the five-layer cuprates Bi2245 and the result in Fig. 1e to the six-layer cuprate Bi2256 because, as seen in Fig. 1c and Fig. 1e, although OP and IP1 Fermi surface sheets are similar, the size of the IP0 Fermi pocket in Fig. 1e is nearly half of that in Fig. 1c.

issues.claim: Pairing coexists with strong AF order
issues.headline: Strong antiferromagnetic order is assumed, not measured
issues.issue: The coexistence claim rests on NMR in Hg- and Ba-based multilayers (Ref. 29) and on pockets fitted with an AFM mean-field model; no folded band, magnetic probe or bound on the AF transition temperature is shown. Pockets near (π/2, π/2) with suppressed outer-side weight can also arise from short-range AF correlations, YRZ-type pockets or matrix elements, and the intensity analyses are only qualitative.

evidence.quote: arises from the coexistence of pronounced electron correlations and strong antiferromagnetic order in the lightly doped regime.

issues.fix: Test whether pockets are centred exactly on the AFM zone boundary, whether shadow intensity mirrors the pocket across the (π,0)–(0,π) line, whether backside weight and R/L follow mean-field coherence factors quantitatively at ΔMF = 0.68 eV, and whether a non-magnetic model fits equally well; otherwise state AF order is inferred by analogy, tone down the abstract and label the AFM and AFM+SC regions of Fig. 4h as hypothetical.
issues.fix_scoped: The formation of the Fermi pockets in our Bi-based multilayer cuprates (n=5∼8) is consistent with pronounced electron correlations and antiferromagnetic order in the lightly doped regime, which we infer by analogy with other multilayer cuprates rather than measure directly.

edit_scoped.before: The formation of the Fermi pockets in our Bi-based multilayer cuprates (n=5∼8) arises from the coexistence of pronounced electron correlations and strong antiferromagnetic order in the lightly doped regime.

issues.claim: Intrinsic metallic state and abrupt transition at infinitesimal doping
issues.headline: 'Abrupt' metallic transition at 'infinitesimal' doping is an extrapolation
issues.issue: No data exist at p = 0 or between 0 and 0.007, and the p = 0.007 point is a single hemispherical-analyser region the authors call less reliable. A coherent peak at 15 K does not by itself establish a metallic ground state (weak localization, AFM-band insulator, small unresolved gap), there is no transport or temperature dependence, and IP0 sits a few ångströms from metallic superconducting outer planes that may stabilize its quasiparticles.

evidence.quote: We observe well-defined Fermi pockets with hole doping levels as low as 0.007, demonstrating an abrupt transition from the parent Mott insulator to a metallic state upon the introduction of an infinitesimal amount of doping.

issues.fix: Quantify IP0 quasiparticle weight and linewidth versus p to see whether Z extrapolates to a finite value, add temperature-dependent data on IP0 weight at EF if possible, discuss the role of the metallic outer planes, and rephrase 'abrupt transition upon infinitesimal doping' as an extrapolation.
issues.fix_scoped: We observe well-defined Fermi pockets with hole doping levels as low as 0.007, showing that at 15 K the lightly doped inner CuO2 planes host coherent quasiparticles at the Fermi level down to this doping, which suggests a rapid crossover from the parent Mott insulator to a metallic state.

edit_scoped.before: We observe well-defined Fermi pockets with hole doping levels as low as 0.007, demonstrating an abrupt transition from the parent Mott insulator to a metallic state upon the introduction of an infinitesimal amount of doping.

issues.headline: Gapless IP0 claim needs a quantitative upper bound on any gap
issues.issue: The IP0 band top lies only ~11 meV above EF at p ≈ 0.01 and closer still at p = 0.007, where a symmetrized EDC can show a peak at EF whether or not a small gap is present; IP0 outer-side peaks are also weak. The gapless-IP0 versus ~12 meV IP1 comparison at p = 0.02 is central to the interpretation.

evidence.quote: all symmetrized EDCs show a peak at the Fermi level, indicating the absence of gap opening along these pockets.

issues.fix: State the smallest resolvable gap given ~1 meV resolution, 15 K and the linewidth; show Fermi–Dirac-divided spectra and leading-edge midpoints along IP0 against gold; show IP0 and IP1 pockets at the same doping in the same region with identical analysis; and discuss why IP0 in a Tc = 111 K crystal shows no proximity-induced gap.
issues.fix_scoped: For both IP0 pockets with doping levels of 0.007 (Fig. 3f) and 0.037 (Fig. 3g), all symmetrized EDCs show a peak at the Fermi level, indicating no gap opening along these pockets within our energy resolution and linewidth.

issues.headline: Conversion from pocket area to doping is unspecified; back side weak
issues.issue: The paper says only that p is determined from the enclosed area, but for AF-reconstructed pockets the result changes by a factor of two with the counting convention, setting the absolute scale and the comparison with Refs. 21, 22. With R/L approaching zero at p ≈ 0.08, the pocket back side and hence the area come largely from a fit or ellipse assumption.

evidence.quote: The hole doping level of the Fermi pocket is determined from its enclosed area.

issues.fix: Give the explicit Luttinger formula and confirm it matches Refs. 21, 22; show measured back-side kF points with uncertainties propagated into p; confirm no other states contribute; add horizontal error bars in Figs. 1h–j, 2h, 3n and 4f; and for one region sum per-plane dopings against the host oxygen content.
issues.fix_scoped: The hole doping level of the Fermi pocket is estimated from its enclosed area; because the back side of the larger pockets is weak, these values carry additional uncertainty.

issues.claim: IP1 d-wave gap up to ~33 meV
issues.headline: IP1 gap magnitudes and doping trend inconsistent between Fig. 3m and 3n
issues.issue: Fig. 3n and the text say the gap decreases toward p = 0.02, yet the d-wave fits give a non-monotonic Δ0 of 46, 30 and 60 meV for p = 0.020, 0.051 and 0.088. On small pockets the 'maximum gap' mostly measures how far the pocket extends toward the antinode, each Δ0 is a two- to four-fold extrapolation assuming a simple d-wave form, and a linear dependence near the node fits many gap forms.

evidence.quote: the component near the Fermi level (marked by ticks) corresponds to the IP1 band, while the higher binding energy component originates from the overlapping IP0 band.

issues.fix: Fit the two components explicitly or choose k-points free of IP0 weight, and show unsymmetrized EDCs with the fit decomposition at the largest-gap angles.

issues.claim: Inner planes disorder-free; insulating behaviour elsewhere due to disorder
issues.headline: 'Disorder-free' inner planes asserted, not demonstrated
issues.issue: No estimate of disorder in the inner planes or disorder-tuned comparison is given, so the statement that insulating behaviour in single- and bilayer cuprates must be re-evaluated is untested. Alternatives such as screening by metallic outer planes and different apical environments are not considered.

evidence.quote: Observations of insulating behavior in single-layer and bilayer cuprates must be re-evaluated in light of strong disorder effects.

issues.fix: Add a quantitative indicator such as the nodal MDC width of IP0 and IP1 compared with OP and with Bi2212 at comparable doping on the same system, consider alternative explanations, and present the argument as a hypothesis unless such evidence is added.

issues.claim: Single t–U parameter set describes all pockets
issues.headline: Mean-field t–U fit is qualitative and cannot address the IP0/IP1 dichotomy
issues.issue: With four parameters fixed and only μ varied against about three cuts per pocket, and dopings derived in the same rigid-band picture, the linear μ(p) largely restates the assumption. Fitting procedure, uncertainties and residuals are not given; ΔMF = 0.68 eV is not related to the ~1 eV charge-transfer gap or Ref. 27; the 2 eV band of Fig. 4a conflicts with the schematic of Fig. 4g; and the model has no pairing term and treats IP0 and IP1 identically.

issues.claim: IP1 gap magnitudes versus earlier reports
issues.headline: Disagreement with Refs. 21, 22 on IP1 gaps not resolved
issues.issue: Kurokawa et al. report gapless IP1 below p = 0.04 and ~5 meV gaps above, whereas this paper finds ~12 meV at p = 0.020 and up to 33 meV, attributed to 'many additional factors'. Differences in doping convention, gap definition, analysis, temperature, resolution and structure are not excluded, and the p = 0.020 point comes from the only hemispherical-analyser region.

evidence.quote: Many additional factors need to be considered including the antiferromagnetic order and interlayer interactions.

issues.fix: Exclude differences in doping convention, gap definition (vertex value vs Δ0), analysis method, temperature and resolution; discuss structural differences (apical F vs O, reservoir layers, IP1–OP spacing); and check the p = 0.020 IP1 point with the ARToF system.
issues.fix_scoped: These contrasting behaviors between IP0 and IP1 pockets, as well as among IP1 pockets in different systems, may partly reflect differences in doping convention, gap definition, analysis and crystal structure, and suggest that gap opening and magnitude are not governed solely by the doping level.
